title: The Statistical Analysis Process & Types of Studies
description: Describe the steps of a statistical investigation and classify a study by its design.
subskills: Identify the population, sample, variable, and research question in a study
Classify a variable as categorical or quantitative
Distinguish an observational study from an experiment
State what kind of conclusion each study type supports
group: Module 1: Statistical Studies and Describing Data

title: Sampling, Bias & Experimental Design
description: Evaluate how data were collected and what the method allows us to conclude.
subskills: Describe random, stratified, cluster, and systematic sampling and select a sample with each
Identify sources of bias in a sampling plan
Explain the roles of random assignment, control groups, and blinding
Decide whether results generalize to a population or support cause and effect
group: Module 1: Statistical Studies and Describing Data

title: Displaying Quantitative Data
description: Build and read dotplots and histograms and describe a distribution.
subskills: Construct a dotplot or histogram from data
Describe shape, center, and spread, and identify outliers
Read counts and percentages from a graph
Compare two distributions in context
group: Module 1: Statistical Studies and Describing Data

title: Measures of Center & Variability
description: Summarize a distribution with a measure of center and a measure of spread, and choose the pair that fits.
subskills: Calculate the mean and median and predict how skew and outliers affect each
Find the five-number summary and interquartile range, construct a boxplot, and identify outliers
Calculate and interpret the standard deviation
Choose measures of center and spread for a distribution and compare groups in context
prerequisites: S-3; order of operations, square roots
group: Module 1: Statistical Studies and Describing Data

title: Probability Basics & Rules
description: Find and interpret probabilities using sample spaces, relative frequencies, and probability rules.
subskills: List a sample space and find the probability of an event
Interpret probability as a long-run relative frequency
Apply the complement and addition rules
Find conditional probabilities from a two-way table and check independence

title: Discrete Random Variables & Expected Value
description: Describe a discrete random variable with its distribution, mean, and standard deviation.
subskills: Decide whether a table is a valid probability distribution
Find probabilities of events from a distribution
Calculate the mean (expected value) and standard deviation
Interpret an expected value in context

title: The Binomial Distribution
description: Recognize binomial settings and compute binomial probabilities.
subskills: Check the conditions for a binomial setting
Find binomial probabilities with a formula or technology
Find the mean and standard deviation of a binomial variable
Use a binomial probability to judge whether an outcome is unusual

title: The Normal Distribution & z-Scores
description: Use areas under a density curve, z-scores, and the standard normal distribution to find probabilities.
subskills: Interpret area under a density curve as probability
Compute and interpret a z-score
Find a normal probability with technology or the Empirical Rule
Find the value that corresponds to a given percentile

title: Sampling Distributions of Sample Proportions
description: Describe how sample proportions vary from sample to sample.
subskills: Distinguish a parameter from a statistic
Describe the shape, center, and spread of the distribution of sample proportions
Check the conditions for a normal model
Find the probability of a sample proportion in a given range

title: Confidence Intervals for a Proportion
description: Estimate a population proportion with a confidence interval.
subskills: Check the conditions for the interval
Calculate the margin of error and the interval
Interpret the interval and the confidence level in context
Explain how sample size and confidence level change the width

title: Hypothesis Tests for a Proportion
description: Test a claim about a population proportion.
subskills: State null and alternative hypotheses for a claim
Calculate the test statistic and P-value
Make a decision at a significance level and state the conclusion in context
Describe Type I and Type II errors and their consequences

title: Sampling Distributions of Sample Means
description: Describe how sample means vary and use the Central Limit Theorem.
subskills: Distinguish the distribution of a population, of a sample, and of sample means
Find the mean and standard deviation of the distribution of sample means
Apply the Central Limit Theorem to decide when a normal model fits
Find the probability of a sample mean in a given range

title: Confidence Intervals for a Mean
description: Estimate a population mean with a t-interval.
subskills: Check the conditions for a t-interval
Find the critical t-value and degrees of freedom
Calculate and interpret the interval in context
Read a confidence interval from technology output

title: Hypothesis Tests for a Mean
description: Test a claim about a population mean with a t-test.
subskills: State hypotheses about a population mean
Calculate the t-statistic and find the P-value
State the conclusion in context
Distinguish statistical significance from practical importance

title: Inference for Paired Samples
description: Analyze paired data through the differences.
subskills: Recognize a paired design and compute the differences
Construct and interpret a confidence interval for the mean difference
Carry out a paired t-test
Explain why pairing changes the analysis

title: Comparing Two Proportions
description: Compare two population proportions with an interval or a test.
subskills: Describe the distribution of differences between sample proportions
Check conditions and state hypotheses
Calculate the test statistic and P-value, or the interval
Interpret the result in context

title: Comparing Two Means & Choosing an Inference Method
description: Compare two population means from independent samples, and select the procedure that fits a research question.
subskills: Distinguish independent samples from paired samples
Carry out a two-sample t-test or interval
Interpret the result and technology output in context
Select the interval or test that fits the variable type and number of groups, and list its conditions

title: One-Way ANOVA
description: Compare three or more population means.
subskills: State the hypotheses for a one-way ANOVA
Explain the F-statistic as variation between groups relative to variation within groups
Read an ANOVA table or technology output to find F and the P-value
State the conclusion in context and what it does not show

title: Scatterplots & Correlation
description: Describe the relationship between two quantitative variables.
subskills: Construct a scatterplot and identify explanatory and response variables
Describe direction, form, and strength
Interpret the correlation coefficient r
Explain why correlation does not establish causation

title: Linear Regression & Correlation Inference
description: Fit a line to data, judge how well it fits, and test whether the relationship is significant.
subskills: Find the line of best fit with technology, interpret slope and intercept, and predict without extrapolating
Calculate and interpret a residual and the coefficient of determination
Test whether a linear correlation is significant using the P-value from technology
Recognize a nonlinear pattern and fit an exponential model with technology
prerequisites: S-11, S-19; slope-intercept form of a line

title: Chi-Square Tests
description: Test a claim about one categorical variable (goodness of fit) or about two (independence, homogeneity).
subskills: Calculate expected counts for a goodness-of-fit test
Calculate the chi-square statistic, find the degrees of freedom and the P-value
Distinguish independence from homogeneity and calculate expected counts for a two-way table
State the conclusion of a chi-square test in context
